findings.problem: After the per-graph bound `hcond`, the proof averages over the graph law. It bounds the local mass by 1 (`hy`), applies `D.drift` and rewrites with `localSet_mass`/`localSet_cost`. It then uses `B_le_one` to weaken `B x*g*V+12ζV` to `(g+12ζ)*V` (`hVB`, `nlinarith`), multiplies by `h` and closes with `linarith`. `CopyState.roundLaw_drift` in Process/PhysicalState.lean repeats this almost line for line (lines 106–125). The only differences are `μ` versus `μ.real`, `s.2 j` versus `S`, and `client j` versus `client`. The reasoning is the generator-drift-to-step-drift conversion, including the `B ≤ 1` weakening. It is not a short calculation. A fix to any of these steps must currently be made twice.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma in Process/PhysicalState.lean, next to `roundLaw_drift`, and use it in both proofs. Its statement would be: for `D : Taper.GraphData Δ g P (fun i : s.1 => location i.val.1) (own Δ s.1)`, `μ : FiniteLaw (s.1 → Finset s.1)`, `S ⊆ s.1` and `S ⊆ S₀` with `mass g S₀ = 1`, a client `c`, `b`, `E : (s.1 → Finset s.1) → ℝ` and constants `f c₀`, assume `hcond : ∀ G, 0 < μ.weight G → E G ≤ f + h*(a + chargeSum G) + c₀`, where `a`/`chargeSum` are the same lets. Also assume the existing hypotheses `hg hunit hP0 hP1 hx0 hx1 hh0 hζ0 hζ1 he hfirst hpair`. Conclude `μ.expect E ≤ f + h*(g+12*ζ)*PhysicalPotential.cost g (fun i => dist c (location i.1)) S + c₀`. The proof is the shared block: `expect_mono_support`, the `simp_rw` expectation lemmas, `hy`, `D.drift`, the `localSet_*` rewrites, `hVB`, `nlinarith`, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left`, `linarith`. In `roundLaw_drift`, call it with `μ`, `client j`, `s.2 j` and `E := fun G => law.expect …`, then finish with `roundLaw`/`expect_bind`/`expect_map`. In `step_drift`, call it with `μ.real` and `E := fun G => (ν G).real.expect (v G)`, then finish with `step_expectation` and `real_expect_all`. Each caller then keeps only its own `hcond` proof (the call to `conditional_round_drift` or `rational_conditional_round_drift`) and its own final coercion.
findings.benefit: The roughly 20-line averaging argument, which includes the `B ≤ 1` weakening, would be stated and proved once. Each user theorem would shrink to its specific per-graph bound plus its own law-coercion step. Future changes to the drift constants or to `D.drift` would be made in one place instead of two. Reading `step_drift` would also be easier, since it would no longer mix the algebra of the generator with the rational-law bookkeeping.
